# cycle_scheduler_service (Resource)

Manages the scheduler service for a Cycle environment. The scheduler is an environment singleton used by function-strategy containers. Create and update send a `reconfigure` job. There is no dedicated GET endpoint; Terraform reads `services.scheduler` from `GET /v1/environments/{id}`.

High availability is not part of the reconfigure job body and is always `false` as of the Cycle API. **Destroy is a state-only no-op.** Removing this resource from Terraform does not disable or reconfigure the Cycle scheduler service.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The scheduler is an environment singleton used by function containers.
# Destroy only drops Terraform state; the Cycle scheduler service remains.
resource "cycle_scheduler_service" "api" {
  environment_id = cycle_environment.api.id
  auto_update    = true

  config = jsonencode({
    public = false
  })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `environment_id` (String) The ID of the environment whose scheduler service is managed. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.

### Optional

- `auto_update` (Boolean) Whether the scheduler service container is set to auto-update.
- `config` (String) Scheduler configuration as a JSON object (`SchedulerConfig`). Fields: `public` (bool) and optional `access_keys`.

### Read-Only

- `container_id` (String) The ID of the scheduler service container, if one has been provisioned.
- `enable` (Boolean) Whether the scheduler service is currently enabled.
- `high_availability` (Boolean) Whether the scheduler service is running in high availability mode. The Cycle API reports this as always `false`.
- `id` (String) The environment ID this scheduler service belongs to. The service is a singleton keyed on `environment_id`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The scheduler service is imported using the environment ID.
terraform import cycle_scheduler_service.api 651efd54c53f7b6e2c5a9f21
```
